about.what: Every property this builder knows, and what is true of each. Nothing reads this file yet -- it is the vocabulary, recorded so that tests/properties.js can hold the rest of the repository to it. Behaviour comes later; see docs/TODO.md.
about.why: Before this file there was no list. formatObjects.formatProperties named 42 keys, the component rule files named 31, the templates read 39, and the built output carried 65. Nothing reconciled them, so a property could be declared by a rule file and read by nobody, read by a template and set by nobody, or typed into a brief and silently dropped.
about.scopes: `entity` is a property that sits directly on a module, a component or a structural node. `content` is inside an entity's `content` object. `segment` is one entry of a text component's `text_segments`; `segment_properties` is that entry's `properties`.
about.node_kinds: module, structure, container, gridContainer, gridRow, gridCol, text, image, button. The last three are components, split by `type` because they render through three different templates and carry three different property sets.

fields.kind: identity (what the thing is), structure (where it sits and what it holds), styling (how it looks), content (what it says), campaign (facts about the send rather than the thing).
fields.value: reference, keyword, text, flag, number, length, spacing, colour, list, object. The shape the value takes. No coercion is wired to these yet; they are here so that when one is, it is written once.
fields.set_by: author (a brief, a rule file or a layout writes it), engine (derived during a build and never authored), both.
fields.applies_to: The node kinds observed carrying it in tests/golden/expected and tests/layouts/expected. Observed, not enforced -- a property may be read on a kind that never carries it, which is exactly the gap several notes below record.
fields.aliases: Other spellings a brief may use, as processing/setup.js correctSpelling() accepts them today.
fields.unused: Present only on a property that nothing sets or nothing reads, and says which. tests/properties.js asserts this both ways: an unused property must have no evidence behind it, and a property with evidence must not be marked unused.
fields.note: Anything a reader would otherwise have to rediscover.

entity_type.note: "module" or "component". main.njk branches on it before it branches on `type`.

block.note: Names the layout template: main.njk includes `layouts/<block>.njk`. Written by the constructors in systems/layout.js and by processing/structureEDM.js.

structure.note: Always the string "structure". It marks the wrapper node structureEDM.js:236 builds, which carries this, `name` and `uuid` and nothing else -- which is why structure.njk still answers for background and padding.

name.note: On a module or component it picks the rule file. On a structural node it is a label: "module container", "block row", and gridContainer.njk renders it into the `name` attribute.

moduleName.note: The designer's own name for the row, from the brief. Not `name`, which is the module type.

category.note: From the `properties` block in libraries/modules.json. Half of `template`.

type.note: On a component it chooses the template -- image, button, or neither, which renders as text.

template.note: `category/name.js`, the rule file that configures the item. tests/golden attributes each difference to the nearest ancestor carrying it.

fragment.note: From libraries/modules.json. A fragment renders from a hand-written .njk instead of from a layout.

nav_label.note: Read only by gridContainer.njk, though rows and columns carry it too.

id.unused: Nothing sets it. image-component.njk:2 and text-component.njk:6 both render it into a `name` attribute, so 313 elements across the nine golden cases ship `name=""`.

layout.unused: Nothing sets it. container.njk:1 renders it into a `name` attribute, so every one of the 22 containers ships `name=""`.

parent_uuid.unused: Declared by formatObjects.js:10, never assigned. It is always null, and utils/style utilities.js cleanUp() strips it before anything is written.

innerLayout.note: "single_row" on a container, "single_column" on a row: the level below is implied rather than written. The only camelCase property in the vocabulary.

position.note: Which slot of a layout the component belongs to -- "top", "bottom", "all". Read by systems/setComponents.js, not by any template.

depth.note: 2 means the module is wrapped in a `container` node. The two aliases are inverses of each other: setup.js formatUserInput() turns `container: false` and `no_container: true` into depth 1.

max_siblings.note: How many of this module may share a row. Read by systems/groupingSystem.js.

mobile_stack.note: Only `false` does anything: gridCol.njk:5 emits `display: table-cell !important` to stop the column stacking.

placeholder_component.note: Renders a zero-height spacer before the node. main.njk checks it in two places and transition-component.njk in a third.

ignore.note: Read by main.njk:200, which renders the node's children without the node, and by processing/applyModifications.js identity(). No recorded case sets it, so it appears in no artifact; footer/signoff petbarn.js writes it for transactional sends.

palette.note: What was asked for. properties/palette.js turns it into `resolved_palette`, `colour` and `background`.

colour.note: The foreground. A palette name resolves to a hex value before rendering.

background.note: Every text rule file declares it null rather than "transparent", which is why two fallbacks in text-component.njk are still load-bearing.

padding.note: The most widely carried property in the vocabulary. On an image or button component systems/setComponents.js copies it onto the wrapping gridCol, so the component's own template never reads it.

margin.note: text-component.njk:4 renders it as the td's padding, not as a margin.

inner_padding.note: Padding inside the clickable area of a button, and inside a badge.

container_padding.note: Becomes the `padding` of the container node structureEDM.js:46 wraps the module in.

group_padding.note: The one spacing property formatObjects does not normalise: its formatSpacingToString call is commented out at formatObjects.js:40.

vertical_align.note: Renders only on a gridCol. All nine component rule files declare it and 362 of the 369 components in the golden cases carry it, where no component template reads it.

align.note: Horizontal placement of the element itself. text-component.njk reads it only as a fallback for `text_align`.

text_align.note: All 78 buttons carry it, 11 of them "left", and button-component.njk never reads it -- it hardcodes `text-align: center` in three places. image-component.njk does not read it either.

height.note: Always "auto" in the recorded cases; `mso_height` carries the real number.

mso_height.note: Separate from `height` because Outlook's <v:roundrect> needs an explicit height where the HTML wants auto.

border_radius.note: container.njk reads it on a container node, which never carries it: every one of the 22 containers takes the template's 24px.

border_top.note: A colour, or false for no border. Width and style are fixed in the template.

border_colour.unused: Declared by formatObjects.js:52, never assigned and never read. The four `border_<side>` properties carry the colour instead.

font.note: A family name, rendered as `'<font>', Arial, sans-serif`.

font_size.note: Derived from `mode` when the author does not set it; an explicit value wins. See ADR 0005.

mode.note: On text a heading level -- h1 to h7, or "default". On a button a shape: "underline" is a different element, not a value that was left out.

text_size_class.note: Derived from the resolved `font_size`, and names a class in main.njk's mobile media query.

force_mso_colour.note: Suppresses the `mso-color-alt` declaration Outlook would otherwise apply.

transition.note: The previous module's background without its hash, or false. structureEDM.js sets it when two adjacent modules differ, and transition-component.njk draws the wobble between them.

content.note: Two shapes under one name. On a module or a text component it is a plain string, the copy itself. On an image or a button it is an object -- the `content` scope below -- and the string, if there is one, is inside it as `text`.

text_segments.note: Rich text from systems/richTextSystem.js. See the `segment` scope below.

subject_line.note: Read by main.njk from content[0], so it only matters on the first module.

dynamicContent.note: Spaces become underscores. setup.js fills it from `versions` or `inVersions`, whichever the brief template offers.

inVersions.note: A brief column, kept on the entity after setup.js has copied it into `dynamicContent`.

transactional.note: Set on every module by setup.js:33 when the first row says so. Four footers and a signoff branch on it at layout time. No recorded case sets it, so it appears in no artifact.

no_nav.note: Read by header/header greencross vets.js:118 to drop the nav row. No recorded case sets it.

hpp.note: Read by footer/footer greencross vets.js:96 to add the Healthy Pets Plus terms. No recorded case sets it.

debug.note: Read from content[0] by main.njk, which outlines every container in colour.

user_settings.note: What the brief's Settings and Styling cells said, kept so layers 5 and 6 of ADR 0005 can be re-applied after every pass. Its keys are not validated against this file -- that is the next step.

text.note: Only a button keeps its copy here. A text component's copy is the `content` string itself.

href.note: On an image it wraps the in a link; 293 of the 406 recorded images have one.

aem_id.note: The asset's id in AEM, rendered as `data-medialibrary-id`. 280 of 406 images have one; image-component.njk still answers for the rest.
